advisories.summary: Collabora Collabora Online – Built-in CODE Server when used within the NextCloud platform contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows for remote code execution when the CODE server isn't running.

advisories.title: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL Injection Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator on-prem contains a SQL injection vulnerability that may allow a remote attacker to access privileged internal functionality and impact the VCO host. Successful exploitation may compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the orchestrator and data managed by the orchestrator.

advisories.title: PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability
advisories.summary: PHP contains a stale internal request-state vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.

advisories.title: PHP Memory Corruption Vulnerability
advisories.summary: PHP contains an out-of-memory corruption vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution.

advisories.title: Google Brotli Unchecked Return Value Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Google Brotli contains an unchecked return value vulnerability that allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream.

advisories.title: Adobe Commerce and Magento Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Adobe Commerce and Magento contain an unrestricted upload of file with dangerous type vulnerability that could result in arbitrary code execution in the context of the current user, potentially gaining elevated access or control over the victim's account or session.

advisories.title: Linux Kernel Missing Initialization of a Variable Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Linux Kernel contains a missing initialization of a variable vulnerability that could allow for unintended modification of page-cache-backed data via failure to preserve the shared-fragment marker during socket buffer coalescing, causing ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root.

advisories.title: Broadcom VMWare ESX Insufficient Logging Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Broadcom VMWare ESX contains an insufficient logging vulnerability that could allow a malicious actor with admin access to perform certain operations without being logged.

advisories.title: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software Unchecked Return Value to NULL Pointer Dereference Vulnerability
advisories.product: Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software
advisories.summary: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software contains an unchecked return value to NULL pointer dereference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition.

advisories.title: GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition Integer Overflow or Wraparound Vulnerability
advisories.summary: GitLab Community Edition and Enterprise Edition contain a integer overflow or wraparound vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation.

advisories.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Ivanti Connect Secure contains a missing authentication for critical function vulnerability that could allow a local authenticated attacker to escalate their privileges. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-118527.

advisories.title: Ivanti Connect Secure Generation of Predictable Numbers or Identifiers Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Ivanti Connect Secure contains a generation of predictable numbers or identifiers vulnerability that allows a remote authenticated attacker to upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-111357.

advisories.title: WordPress WordPress Core Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition Vulnerability
advisories.summary: WordPress WordPress Core contains a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during the upgrade window. This is due to predictable, web-accessible staging paths used during full-package core upgrades.

advisories.title: Apple Multiple Products Improper Authentication Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Apple iOS, iPadOS, macOS, Safari, tvOS and watchOS 10.5 contain an improper authentication vulnerability which could allow an attacker with arbitrary read and write capability to bypass pointer authentication.

advisories.title: SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN Use of Single-factor Authentication Vulnerability
advisories.summary: SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN contains a use of single-factor authentication vulnerability that may allow a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML authentication controls. Successful exploitation may also bypass SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication (MFA).

advisories.title: IBM Aspera Faspex Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability
advisories.summary: IBM Aspera Faspex contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that could allow an authenticated user to craft a specific message to bypass authorization, causing privilege escalations.

advisories.title: SignalWire FreeSwitch Code Injection Vulnerability
advisories.summary: SignalWire FreeSwitch contains a code injection vulnerability that permits configuration and credential disclosure, arbitrary call control, and command execution.

advisories.title: OpenBSD OpenSSH Unexpected Status Code or Return Value Vulnerability
advisories.summary: OpenBSD OpenSSH on Linux contains an unexpected status code or return value vulnerability that could allow for authentication bypass.

advisories.title: GPUStack Improper Authentication Vulnerability
advisories.summary: GPUStack contains an improper authentication vulnerability which could allow unauthenticated administrative access, including user and model changes, persistent administrator API-key creation, disclosure of worker and cloud-provider secrets, and code execution through POST /v2/inference-backends/from-yaml.

advisories.title: Google Chromium Use-After-Free Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Google Chromium contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XML component that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the sandbox via a specially crafted webpage. This vulnerability could affect multiple web browsers that utilize Chromium, including, but not limited to, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Opera.

advisories.title: Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to invoke a configuration-import function and restore a crafted, compatible backup archive, resulting in unauthorized modification of the appliance’s global configuration. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-111560.

advisories.title: Barracuda Networks Multiple Products OS Command Injection Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG), Load Balancer, Application Delivery Controller (ADC), Message Archiver (BMA), WAF Control Center (WCC), Web Application Firewall (WAF), and Web Security Gateway (WSG) contain an OS command injection vulnerability. This vulnerability could allow an authenticated administrator to inject OS commands that execute with root privileges when the crafted timezone value is subsequently processed. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-116606

advisories.title: Cisco BroadWorks Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Cisco BroadWorks contains an improper restriction of XML external entity reference vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to read sensitive configuration information on an affected system.

advisories.title: Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder contains an incorrect resource transfer between spheres vulnerability that may allow an authenticated user to process and convert unintended document types if bypassing the Webmail experience.

advisories.title: Microsoft Office Outlook Missing User Interaction for Potentially Unsafe Action Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Microsoft Office Outlook contains a missing user interaction for potentially unsafe action vulnerability that allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

advisories.title: Check Point Multiple Products Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Check Point Firewall, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Scalable Platforms, Security Gateway, and Security Management Server contain an incorrect permissions assignment for critical resources vulnerability when the Gaia OS DynamicCLI daemon runs as root and listens on a world-writable local socket without authenticating connecting processes. An authenticated local user can send a command to the socket and have it executed as root.

advisories.title: UnrealIRCd Improper Neutralization of Delimiters Vulnerability
advisories.summary: UnrealIRCd UnrealIRCd contains an improper neutralization of delimiters vulnerability that allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority.

advisories.title: Perforce Puppet Enterprise Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Puppet’s report-processing code that allows a client with any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type through a PUT request. If the certificate authority automatically signs requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a valid certificate and exploit the vulnerability.

advisories.title: Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Apache Axis contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via a crafted SOAP fault message that causes Axis to load and instantiate an attacker-specified class when a suitable class is available on the application classpath. The impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.

advisories.title: Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) contains a code injection vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server. An attacker could exploit this via crafted HTTP requests that access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and supply a crafted file-path or stream parameter during data import processing. Exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash.

advisories.title: BerriAI LiteLLM Unprotected Alternate Channel Vulnerability
advisories.summary: BerriAI LiteLLM contains an unprotected alternate channel vulnerability that could allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary code via bytecode rewriting at the /guardrails/test_custom_code URI.

advisories.title: Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Synology DSM contains an improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in the system plugin daemon in Synology BeeStation OS (BSM) that could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via unspecified vectors.

advisories.title: Cisco Expressway Series Use of Hard-coded Credentials Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Cisco Expressway Series contains a use of hard-coded credentials vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker with persistent cookies and network access to execute commands as root on a clustered device via the database service.

advisories.title: SAP NetWeaver Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic Vulnerability
advisories.summary: SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal contains an improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated attacker to disclose or modify server information via injected JNDI environment properties or a URL used during JNDI lookup operations.

advisories.title: VMWare vCenter Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Broadcom VMware vCenter contains an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel vulnerability in the VMware Directory Service that allows an unauthenticated attacker with network access to vCenter to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system.

advisories.title: Apache Roller Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
advisories.summary: Apache Roller contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code via the XML-RPC endpoint, which accepts and deserializes vendor extension types before authentication. This CVE covers the same underlying vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384 but applies to a broader range of affected versions.

updates.body:
On June 23, 2026, following a global software deployment, we identified an issue causing intermittent boot failures specifically for GPU Linodes. The impact was limited to instances where multiple GPU Linodes attempted to boot simultaneously. During the impact window customers could have experienced localized disruption or elevated error rates, particularly during automated node recycling or scaling events.

During the investigation it was found that a recent software update created a conflict when multiple GPU servers tried to start up at the exact same time. The servers essentially blocked one another from loading, and our system did not automatically trigger a retry. This specific interaction only happens under heavy, simultaneous workloads, which is why it wasn't caught during our standard pre-release testing.

In order to mitigate the issue, we successfully deployed a hotfix directly to all active GPU hosts across our fleet at 20:32 UTC on June 24th, 2026. The affected systems are currently operating normally as expected.

In order to prevent this issue from happening in the future, we have developed and integrated a comprehensive fix into our upcoming software release scheduled to roll out globally over the next week. Additionally, we are actively prioritizing the procurement of dedicated GPU testing hardware for our development cloud to improve test coverage and ensure concurrent hardware workloads are fully simulated before future updates reach production.

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
On June 30, 2026, between approximately 17:30 UTC and 21:45 UTC, users may have experienced connection timeouts and errors related to the Block Storage service in Singapore Expansion, SP \(sg-sin-2\).

The issue began when one host in the cluster was taken down for maintenance while another host unexpectedly encountered network issues. A configuration issue also contributed to the impact. These factors led to a degraded state that affected performance and, to a limited extent, data availability. We mitigated the impact to customers at 21:45 UTC on June 30, 2026 by correcting the network, configuration and cluster issues.

We apologize for the impact and appreciate your patience and ongoing support. We are making configuration and operational changes to our systems to help prevent this from happening again, and remain committed to continuous improvement.

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident, given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing, and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body: Our team is investigating a service issue that affects the auto configuration of networking on Linodes by Network Helper to fail. During that time, some users may have Linodes provision but appear to have no connectivity. This also can impact Linodes created by the Linode Kubernetes Engine and impact autoscaling or provisioning of clusters. Customers can still manually configure networking via the LISH console to mitigate this issue. Please see our guide on manual network configuration on a Compute Instance. We will share additional updates as we have more information.

updates.body:
Akamai is aware of the recently disclosed “DirtyFrag”[1] vulnerability that followed the “CopyFail”[2] disclosure.  This vulnerability is very similar in nature and has a similar impact, exploit path, and mitigation approach.  We have not observed any related malicious exploits targeting our infrastructure and are continuing to address the vulnerability across our product portfolio and internal systems.

As with “CopyFail”, we are advising customers to consider most Linux distributions to be at-risk until patched.  Since the “DirtyFrag” vulnerability was disclosed prior to upstream patches having been made available, we are forced to wait for the different OS providers to create new releases or patches before we can integrate them into the versions we make available to customers.

As this is a rapidly developing incident, we will provide further information regarding recommended actions, possible mitigations, and OS updates for all customers who may be affected.

[1] https://github.com/V4bel/dirtyfrag/blob/master/assets/write-up.md
[2] https://www.linode.com/docs/guides/cve-2026-31431-copy-fail-mitigation/

incident_updates.body:
Akamai is aware of the recently disclosed “DirtyFrag”[1] vulnerability that followed the “CopyFail”[2] disclosure.  This vulnerability is very similar in nature and has a similar impact, exploit path, and mitigation approach.  We have not observed any related malicious exploits targeting our infrastructure and are continuing to address the vulnerability across our product portfolio and internal systems.

As with “CopyFail”, we are advising customers to consider most Linux distributions to be at-risk until patched.  Since the “DirtyFrag” vulnerability was disclosed prior to upstream patches having been made available, we are forced to wait for the different OS providers to create new releases or patches before we can integrate them into the versions we make available to customers.

As this is a rapidly developing incident, we will provide further information regarding recommended actions, possible mitigations, and OS updates for all customers who may be affected.

[1] https://github.com/V4bel/dirtyfrag/blob/master/assets/write-up.md
[2] https://www.linode.com/docs/guides/cve-2026-31431-copy-fail-mitigation/

incident_updates.body:
Akamai is aware of the recently disclosed “Fragnesia”[1] vulnerability, following the “DirtyFrag”[2] and “CopyFail”[3] disclosures.  This vulnerability is very similar in nature and has a similar impact, exploit path, and mitigation approach.  We have not observed any related malicious exploits targeting our infrastructure and are continuing to address the vulnerability across our product portfolio and internal systems.

As with “CopyFail” and “DirtyFrag”, we are advising customers to consider most Linux distributions to be at-risk until patched.  Since the “Fragnesia” vulnerability was disclosed prior to upstream patches having been made available, we are forced to wait for the different OS providers to create new releases or patches before we can integrate them into the versions we make available to customers.

As this is a rapidly developing incident, we will provide further information regarding recommended actions, possible mitigations, and OS updates for all customers who may be affected.

[1] https://github.com/v12-security/pocs/tree/main/fragnesia 
[2] https://github.com/V4bel/dirtyfrag/blob/master/assets/write-up.md 
[3] https://www.linode.com/docs/guides/cve-2026-31431-copy-fail-mitigation/

updates.body:
On July 9, 2026, at 15:43 UTC, customers were unable to login to [cloud.linode.com](http://cloud.linode.com) using username and password. Customers were getting "wrong password" error message. 

Investigation revealed that the issue was due to an internal certificate issue.

To mitigate the impact, we fixed the certificate issue on the impacted servers at 17:24 UTC on July 9, 2026. After monitoring our systems for some time, we confirmed the issue was fully resolved.

Akamai will deploy a permanent fix to prevent a recurrence of the issue.

updates.body:
On July 14, 2026, at 10:57 UTC, Akamai identified an increase in 502 errors and latency affecting customers using the Linode API, CLI, and Cloud Manager. This disruption resulted in moderate service impact, with customers reporting elevated error rates. Our initial investigation traced the issue to latency with IAM services, which was resolved, but elevated errors persisted. 

Further analysis by relevant subject matter experts determined that the incident was triggered by a manual failback to the Cloud IAM primary load balancer from the secondary load balancer. This action was prompted by a warning alert indicating that the secondary load balancer was acting as the keepalived master. The manual process of starting and stopping services to initiate the failback differed from the automated process and led to a cascade of stale GRPC connections, causing increased latency and API errors. Restarting the API servers cleared the stale connections and restored normal operations. Customer impact was mitigated by approximately 13:10 UTC on July 14, 2026.

To prevent recurrence, Akamai is investigating why the manual failback caused this behavior. The team is considering implementing a drain command to clear GRPC connections during failover and setting up alerts to detect stale connections for proactive intervention. However, the immediate focus remains on understanding the root cause, with alerting and automation planned for later phases.

Several customers have confirmed resolution across their deployments. Akamai will continue to monitor system health and await additional customer feedback before declaring full recovery. 

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
Our team investigated an issue that affected connectivity in our US-MIA (Miami) data center between 21:20 UTC and approximately 23:28 UTC on July 15, 2026. During this window, users may have experienced degraded networking performance and packet loss for Compute services deployed in this region.

 The issue was resolved after we implemented a fix. We are continuing to work with our third-party service provider to confirm the root cause, as initial evidence points to a campus cross-connect (dark fiber) outage on their infrastructure.

updates.body:
On July 18, 2026, between approximately 00:30 UTC and 04:00 UTC, users might have experienced 5xx errors while trying to create a new bucket in the Object Storage for the following endpoints.

* [us-ord-1.linodeobjects.com](http://us-ord-1.linodeobjects.com)
* [us-lax-1.linodeobjects.com](http://us-lax-1.linodeobjects.com)
* [us-iad-1.linodeobjects.com](http://us-iad-1.linodeobjects.com)
* [us-sea-1.linodeobjects.com](http://us-sea-1.linodeobjects.com)
* [fr-par-1.linodeobjects.com](http://fr-par-1.linodeobjects.com)

‌The issue began when the infrastructure supporting Object Storage entered a degraded state across all nodes. This prevented the service from processing requests, resulting in failures during bucket creation operations.

‌To mitigate the impact, we have applied a fix at the backend system responsible for bucket creation. The impact was mitigated following this action.

‌Our subject matter experts are investigating the root cause and will take appropriate preventive actions.

‌We apologize for the impact and appreciate your patience and ongoing support. We are making configuration and operational changes to our systems to help prevent this from happening again, and remain committed to continuous improvement.

‌This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident, given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing, and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body: Starting around 00:33 UTC on July 20, 2026, some hosts in the Milan, Italy data center became unavailable, impacting customer access to Linodes. The investigation identified that this issue occurred during scheduled router firmware updates. While we follow a phased upgrade process to prevent service disruption, an unexpected intersection of concurrent maintenance activities led to a temporary loss of network connectivity for the affected hosts.   Service was fully restored by 02:16 UTC on July 20, 2026, and all systems are now operating as expected. Internally, we are reviewing our change management and maintenance scheduling procedures to ensure better coordination and prevent similar issues in the future.   We apologize for the impact and thank you for your patience and continued support. We are committed to making continuous improvements to make our systems better and prevent recurrence.   This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing, and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
On 27 July 2026 at 3:30 UTC, Akamai observed an increase in errors when connecting to the Linode hosting database, primarily affecting Block Storage volume attachments. This resulted in host job failures and limited customer impact, with some users experiencing error messages and interrupted workflows. Elevated timeout rates were noted in logs for certain data center locations, coinciding with the incremental rollout of a new feature flag.

Initial investigation revealed intermittent packet drops from the database proxy to client hosts during the TLS handshake. The current theory suggests that a DDoS-protection limit related to path MTU packet too big ICMP messages was reached. When the proxy sent TCP packets with a large MTU, the expected ICMP messages were dropped by Dallas gateway routers due to exceeding the configured allowable rate. This caused database proxy TCP connections to timeout to Compute Hosts. The issue was triggered by the enablement of the new feature flag, which changed the routing path and removed MTU clamping before packets reached the gateways.

To mitigate the issue, Akamai rolled back the recent network change across affected Compute sites, starting at 20:50 UTC. As of 22:57 UTC, the rate of service restarts returned to pre-incident levels. Akamai is also planning a change to increase the allowable threshold for packet too big ICMP messages.

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
On July 31, 2026, at approximately 10:00 UTC, Akamai observed intermittent network losses affecting compute users accessing US locations from our India sites \(MAA and BOM\). Customers’ services in North America, particularly the Miami data center region, experienced increased latency, intermittent connectivity issues, slower data transfers, and difficulty reaching certain applications or services. Performance was unstable, with periods of normal operation followed by disruptions. 

To address the issue, Akamai applied a deny-all policy to the impacted upstream provider transit link, redirecting traffic around the impacted routes. Despite this mitigation, ongoing IPv6 losses occurred due to congestion between two alternative upstream providers, impacting some users. One provider acknowledged a bottleneck in the Asia region, and the alternate provider worked to reroute traffic away from affected links. 

The initial impacted service provider confirmed that two fiber cuts in Mexico caused congestion on the impacted routes. One of these fiber cuts was resolved at 23:43 UTC on July 31, 2026, and no further issues were observed following this mitigation. 

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
On August 13, 2026, between approximately 14:30 and 16:30 UTC, Akamai experienced an issue affecting Linode Kubernetes Engine Enterprise \(LKE-E\) cluster provisioning and deployment in the Seattle \(SEA1\) region. During this time, customers attempting to create new clusters encountered failures or delays. In some cases, clusters were created but nodes were not fully provisioned, while in others, the control plane responsible for managing the cluster could not be deployed.

Akamai identified the issue through customer reports, which was then validated by reproducing the failures in Seattle-based test clusters. Other regions continued to operate normally, and no existing customer workloads were impacted.

By around 16:30 UTC on August 13, 2026, cluster provisioning and deployment in the Seattle region returned to normal, allowing new cluster creations to proceed without issue. After recovery, we monitored the region for several days and began a technical investigation into the service disruption. Initial findings indicate a correlation between the issue and a recent network configuration update that occurred at approximately 14:30 UTC and was rolled back at approximately 14:45 UTC. Our current hypothesis suggests that a timing conflict during the cluster provisioning process may have triggered the failures. We are continuing to investigate the technical details to confirm the root cause.

We are continuing to investigate the technical details behind this issue and are working to ensure it does not recur. We will also review the scope of affected data centers and track corrective actions. 

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
Between 17:25 UTC and 22:50 UTC on August 13, 2026, Linode Kubernetes Engine Enterprise \(LKE-E\) customers attempting to deploy G7 dedicated Linode instances in our Washington \(IAD2\) data center, received 403 provisioning error messages. Active workloads and running instances were not affected by this issue.

Our investigation revealed that while total physical hardware capacity in IAD2 was sufficient, the provisioning request triggered an entitlement check failure due to an initial soft host-allocation threshold.

Akamai resolved the issue by increasing the Linode-per-host limit from 5 to 20 in IAD2. Full deployment capabilities were restored and stabilized at 22:50 UTC.

To prevent recurrence moving forward, we will implement dedicated alerting for entitlement and capacity issues, directly linked to response runbooks for rapid remediation. Additionally, we are building a centralized capacity overview dashboard to proactively track regional headroom.

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
On August 13th, 2026, at approximately 18:15 UTC, Akamai observed a brief service outage affecting [_api.linode.com_](http://api.linode.com). The total service interruption lasted for approximately 3 minutes, concluding at 18:18 UTC. Following the restoration of initial connectivity, elevated API response latency persisted through 19:06 UTC, causing slower response times and intermittent delays for customers interacting with API services.

To address the performance impact, Akamai engineering teams identified a configuration discrepancy on the secondary caching infrastructure node that prevented it from absorbing the full traffic load after the failover. Engineers completed a controlled migration and moved request caching traffic back over to the primary host. Following this change, API latency rapidly decreased to normal operational levels.

The initial condition was triggered by an unexpected reboot of the primary caching node's physical host. While redundant infrastructure was active, the secondary node was unable to process the failover traffic seamlessly, causing the extended performance degradation.

Our engineering teams are conducting a follow-up investigation into the failover mechanisms to optimize execution speeds and align configuration settings across redundant nodes, ensuring secondary systems can handle traffic seamlessly in future events.

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
On August 21, 2026 starting approximately at 17:23 UTC, customers using the Seattle data center \(US-SEA\) were unable to provision new nodes or complete host jobs, whereas customers outside Seattle were unaffected. 

The investigation revealed that this was due to a Linux kernel issue that was triggered on a network router due to increased network traffic at this site while a specific BIOS setting was enabled.  This caused system instability and affected job processing in the US-SEA region.

To mitigate the impact, the Akamai team disabled a problematic setting and rebooted the affected system, restoring service and moving the situation to a monitoring state by 21:59 UTC on August 21, 2026. As preventive actions, Akamai will audit hardware configurations to ensure the problematic feature is explicitly disabled, and implement enhanced monitoring to detect similar issues in the future. 

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
On September 21, 2026, starting at approximately 16:10 UTC, Akamai observed degraded DNS resolution performance affecting a subset of Linode instances within the London \(`LON1`\) region. Platform-wide DNS resolution remained functional, and no other regions were affected.

The disruption occurred during a drive transplant of a compute host at the London \(lon1\) data center, which temporarily took a customer-facing DNS resolver offline. Due to a software logic flaw, customer workload configurations deployed in the last year across the region were disproportionately reliant on this single resolver, causing DNS failures when it became unavailable.

At 21:45 UTC, engineering teams deployed an emergency configuration update to rebalance and reorder active DNS resolver assignments in the region, returning DNS query performance to baseline levels. Post-remediation monitoring confirmed stable operations across `LON1`. 

Long-term engineering updates are currently being deployed to ensure provisioning utilities dynamically assign distinct, active DNS resolvers across all regions to prevent recurrence.

This summary reflects our current understanding of the incident based on available details. Our investigation remains ongoing, and findings may be updated as further information is reviewed.

To prevent this issue from reoccurring, we are modifying our maintenance planning process to ensure that critical components are taken offline in a phased manner that doesn’t introduce customer impact.

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
Starting October 17, 2026, customers were unable to create new Linode Kubernetes Engine-Enterprise \(LKE-E\) clusters globally. The impact was limited to newly provisioned LKE-E clusters, while the existing clusters, ongoing customer workloads, and cluster scaling remained fully functional and were unaffected throughout the event.

Investigation revealed that the impact occurred after Linode Virtual Private Cloud \(VPC\) subnet IDs crossed 1,000,000 \(one million\), following growth on October 17, 2026. Due to a software logic flaw, the Cloud Controller Manager parsed these 7-digit IDs into scientific notation instead of raw integers, rendering the IDs invalid and causing required core components to remain pending on newly created clusters.

To mitigate the issue, Akamai deployed a fix to enforce strict integer formatting and patched existing custom resources to restore the affected clusters. Akamai’s internal testing confirmed that the newly provisioned test clusters were fully operational. With the successful testing, Akamai deployed the fix across the platform, and the impact was considered mitigated at around 19:49 UTC on October 20, 2026.

Akamai is working on the root cause and will take appropriate preventive actions. We apologize for the impact and thank you for your patience and continued support.

This summary reflects our current understanding of the incident based on available details. Our investigation remains ongoing, and findings may be updated as further information is reviewed.

Akamai immediately began investigating the issue and working to correct it. 

We corrected the malformed data at 12:50 UTC on October 22, 2026 and service was restored. 

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing, and any information herein is subject to change.

updates.body:
On October 10, 2026, Akamai became aware of two zero-day remote code execution \(RCE\) vulnerabilities affecting the PHP core engine, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. Akamai began a platform-wide investigation, and deployed global Web Application Firewall \(WAF\) mitigation rules on October 21, 2026, and carried out remediation protocols across potentially impacted infrastructure.

At this time, Akamai has observed no evidence that these vulnerabilities impacted core Akamai products, API calls, or the Akamai Control Center \(ACC\). The potential scope included PHP Core, Linode Speed Test Services, and Quick Deploy Marketplace applications. As a precaution, Akamai temporarily disabled Cloud Infrastructure Speed Tests while teams isolated and rebuilt related systems.

Akamai deployed protective WAF rules across the Akamai edge platform to inspect and mitigate potential exploitation attempts. Marketplace application templates were also updated so new Linode Compute Marketplace deployments automatically use patched PHP packages. The existing customer-managed instances running vulnerable PHP versions require customer action to apply the latest official security updates from the upstream PHP project.

Customers using Akamai App & API Protector or Kona Site Defender should confirm that default protective rule sets are active. Customers running PHP on Linode compute instances or other self-managed infrastructure should update PHP packages as soon as possible. The external asset scans confirmed that Akamai production environments remained secured and protected.

Akamai's public security notice is available [here](https://www.akamai.com/blog/security-research/critical-remote-code-execution-vulnerabilities-php-core).

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing, and any information herein is subject to change.

incidents.title: Customer Security Advisory: OpenSSH Password Authentication Bypass Vulnerability [CVE-2026-123158]

updates.body: Akamai is aware of the password authentication bypass vulnerability affecting certain Linux systems using musl libc that was recently mitigated by an urgent OpenSSH update. Since Alpine Linux is specifically called out as being affected, we wanted to assure customers that Linode’s Alpine images are not affected by this vulnerability. Linodes using password-less provisioning do not have password authentication enabled by default unless customers change this configuration option in sshd_config after launch, while linodes launched using a password do not have any unlocked user accounts with a password hash set to ‘*’. However, we would like to use this opportunity as a reminder for customers to consider disabling password authentication permanently in favor of more secure mechanisms such as SSH keys or SSH CA certificates.

incidents.title: Customer Security Advisory: Critical F5/NGINX Out-of-Band Vulnerabilities

updates.body:
Akamai is aware of the recently published F5/NGINX vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-97205, and CVE-2026-93479), and our teams are actively investigating their potential impact across our platform and infrastructure.

F5 has released out-of-band security patches addressing three critical severity vulnerabilities in NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus. These vulnerabilities may allow unauthenticated attackers to trigger heap buffer overflows, which could cause a denial of service or potential remote code execution if ASLR is bypassed.

If you are running a vulnerable version of NGINX Open Source or NGINX Plus on a Linode instance, we recommend following guidance from F5/NGINX and applying available patches.

We will provide updates as additional information becomes available.

updates.body:
Starting around 07:00 UTC on October 24, 2026, an issue affecting connectivity between our ID-CGK \(Jakarta\) and SG-SIN-2 \(Singapore 2\) was identified. The investigation revealed that the issue was caused by an undersea cable cut affecting the international link capacity, which would have resulted in connection timeouts and/or errors for services deployed in these data centers.

To mitigate the immediate impact while the undersea cable was being repaired, we removed the affected links from production traffic and limited the link capacity; network stability was restored following these actions. The impact was fully mitigated at 17:50 UTC on November 13, 2026, once the undersea cable repairs were finished and all previous changes were reverted.

We apologize for the impact and thank you for your patience and continued support. If you have further questions, please contact us at 855-454-6633 \(\+1-609-380-7100 Intl.\), or send an email to [support@linode.com](mailto:support@linode.com) for assistance.

This summary provides an overview of our current understanding of the incident given the information available. Our investigation is ongoing, and any information herein is subject to change.

- Stuck or delayed creates/forks/restores on Mongo, PG, and MySQL databases. 

Please note that operations related to Managed Databases and App Platform Custom Domains will automatically retry and should complete successfully once the upstream outage is resolved. 

We'll continue to monitor this situation and provide updates. We apologize for the inconvenience.

The issue affecting Kubernetes deployments in the NYC1 region has been resolved. Our investigation found intermittent DNS timeouts affecting a small number of DOKS clusters, with affected worker nodes running on shared-CPU Droplets. This is a documented limitation for latency-sensitive cluster DNS workloads such as CoreDNS.

The affected clusters are currently functional. To reduce the risk of recurrence, we recommend running CoreDNS on non-shared/dedicated CPU node pools and using sufficient CoreDNS replicas. 

If you continue to see DNS failures or NodeNotReady events, please open a support ticket so we can investigate that cluster specifically.

Between Aug 6, 06:42 UTC and 09:08 UTC, customers experienced failures with write operations across multiple DigitalOcean services, including Managed Databases, DOKS, Cloud Firewalls, DNS, Spaces, Block Storage Volumes, and event processing.

Customers attempting to update Cloud Firewall rules, modify DNS records, manage object storage operations, provision or scale DOKS clusters and node pools, and make other infrastructure configuration changes experienced failures. These operations returned errors, preventing customers from managing their resources. Additionally, event processing was delayed or failed during this window, which may have impacted the timeliness of resource status updates and notifications.

The services have recovered and are now operating normally. Customers should no longer experience issues with write operations, configuration changes, or event processing.

We apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused. If you continue to experience issues with any of these services, please don't hesitate to open a support ticket. Our team will be happy to assist you.

updates.body:
## 1. What happened

Between 16:56 UTC and 23:09 UTC on August 24, 2026, customers using DigitalOcean’s Cloud Control Panel, Public API, and dependent product management systems experienced elevated request error rates, peaking at 25%, in two distinct windows totaling 3.5 hours of active degradation within a 6-hour span. Running Droplets, network routing, and block storage \(Volumes\) remained fully functional and unaffected throughout the event. No customer data loss occurred.

The event was initiated during a planned infrastructure migration of the database layer supporting identity, authentication, and authorization services. The migration introduced increased execution latency for a critical authorization query. In response to the elevated query latency, multiple upstream services initiated automated hedged retries. This secondary request amplification led to queue buildup in excess of the authentication service pool's processing throughput, resulting in cascading request timeouts across the authorization path.

To mitigate the initial degradation, engineering teams rerouted authorization traffic onto a single healthy processing path and temporarily disabled hedging for primary callers, successfully restoring service availability. However, upon returning traffic to the standard multipath routing configuration, lingering query latency combined with retry behavior from unhedged callers caused recurrent queue saturation, leading to the second window of degradation.

## 2. Impact

* Active customer accounts \(<2%\) experienced one or more API or Control Panel request failures during the event windows.
* Aggregate failure rates across both impact windows averaged approximately 10% of authenticated requests, with a peak error rate of 25% during the second window.
* Affected management control planes included the Cloud Control Panel, Public API, Kubernetes cluster authentication, Container Registry, and Serverless / AI Inference endpoints.
* Data plane components—including active Droplets, network routing, and block storage volumes—maintained 100% availability, as established connections do not depend on the affected authorization control path. There was zero data loss.

## 3. Current state

All impacted control plane services have been restored to nominal operational capacity. The database infrastructure migration has been completed. Remediation controls have been validated to ensure system stability against similar query latency scenarios.

## 4. Preventing recurrence

To prevent future occurrences and enhance systemic resilience, DigitalOcean has implemented the following technical enhancements:

1. Automated Request Throttling and Circuit Breaking:

Deployed automated circuit breakers across upstream services to detect downstream dependency degradation and automatically suppress hedged/retry amplification. Completed a broad architecture audit to ensure retry suppression and circuit breaking are uniformly enforced across all control plane services.

1. Queue Management and Load Shedding:

Implemented fast-fail load-shedding mechanisms to prevent request queue saturation during dependency slowness, accompanied by proactive telemetry alerts to identify queue backing prior to customer impact.

1. Graceful Service Degradation:

Configured critical authorization components to operate in degraded execution modes utilizing asynchronous, eventually-consistent data replicas during primary database latency events.

## 5. Timeline

| **Time UTC** | **Event** |
| --- | --- |
| 16:56 | A specific authorization query began running significantly slower than its historical baseline. |
| 16:58 | Automated monitoring detected abnormal error rates and latency; detected within 5 minutes of impact starting. |
| 17:05–18:52 | Operators tuned retry configuration and consolidated requests to a healthy service instance \(first unavailability window closed\). |
| 21:30 | Shifting traffic back to the production pattern caused the same saturation problem \(second unavailability window begins\). |
| 21:30–23:09 | Teams disabled the retry/amplification behavior across the remaining affected services and added additional read capacity for the slow query. Service was restored to a stable state. |

incidents.title: A Network Disruption in BLR1 Region Impacted Multiple Products (Resolved)

updates.body:
From 11:59 UTC to 13:02 UTC on October 3, 2026, a networking disruption in our BLR1 region affected multiple products, including Monitoring, App Platform, Managed Databases, Functions, Load Balancers, Spaces, and the Cloud Control Panel. During this period, some users experienced degraded connectivity, increased latency, or intermittent errors when accessing resources in the region.

Multiple network paths operated by our upstream connectivity providers were unavailable, including redundant paths intended to maintain connectivity during a disruption. Traffic shifted to a remaining link with insufficient capacity to handle the full load, resulting in network saturation and the connectivity issues described above. Our Engineering and Network teams worked closely with our upstream providers to restore normal routing and connectivity. All affected services have since returned to normal operation.

We apologize for the disruption and its impact on your work. If you continue to experience unexpected behavior, please open a support ticket so our team can investigate and assist you.

We advise customers to set an MSS clamp on their egress traffic in order to ensure ingress traffic is correctly sized.

updates.body: On October 1, 2026, between 13:04 UTC and 13:34 UTC, users experienced two periods of slow page loads and intermittent request failures on GitHub.com. On average, the error rate was 0.52% and peaked at 6.13%. An unusually high volume of incoming traffic placed additional load on our traffic-handling infrastructure, delaying requests before they reached our application servers. Performance returned to normal as the traffic subsided, and we have since applied additional traffic filtering to protect against similar traffic. We are improving alerting for delays in our traffic-handling infrastructure and strengthening our automated traffic protections to reduce our time to detection and mitigation.

updates.body:
On October 1, 2026, GitHub Actions experienced two periods of delayed and failed job starts on GitHub-hosted runners, beginning at approximately 14:15 UTC. Across the 14:15–17:56 UTC incident-response window, approximately 0.68% of workflow runs experienced start delays, and 0.196% of jobs failed to start.

A routing change at our cloud provider concentrated API traffic on a single backend, causing an increase in rate-limit errors. Incorrect retry behavior in the provider’s inventory service added load to the affected APIs, compounding the rate limiting. This disrupted runner provisioning and reduced available capacity in affected regions. The resulting increase in demand in unaffected regions exposed a concurrency limit in our job-assignment system, delaying jobs even where runners were available.

During the response, we increased job-assignment concurrency, scaled runner capacity, and worked with our cloud provider to reduce API load by excluding our runner subscriptions from its inventory service. By approximately 16:15 UTC, jobs were starting and executing as expected. We continued mitigation and monitoring until the incident was resolved at 17:56 UTC.

Our cloud provider has since increased resource-management API rate limits for our workloads. To reduce the likelihood and impact of similar incidents, we are also adding more granular rate-limiting alerts and updating our job-assignment system to handle increased demand across fewer available regions.

On October 5, 2026, between 18:48 and 22:49 UTC, GitHub Actions and Hosted Runners experienced degraded performance. Over the full incident, 14.3% of workflow runs using GitHub-hosted runners and 26.5% of individual GitHub-hosted jobs did not start within five minutes.


During the roughly 90-minute period of highest impact, 47.0% of workflow runs using GitHub-hosted runners failed and 71.9% of GitHub-hosted jobs did not start within five minutes, while existing Pages sites continued to serve normally. A portion of customers also encountered intermittent errors in repository lists, licensing and billing pages, and some Copilot features. Self-hosted runners were not affected.


The incident was caused by a partial networking failure that disrupted connectivity between one of our on-premises datacenter regions and a subset of cloud-hosted regional database and storage services.


We mitigated the incident by shifting database and storage traffic to healthy regions and endpoints and increasing capacity for affected compute services. GitHub Actions and Hosted Runners recovered by 21:54 UTC, and all affected services recovered by 22:49 UTC.


We are partnering with our cloud provider to understand the network failure and identify improvements to network-path resilience, detection, and recovery for similar incidents.

updates.body:
On October 6, 2026, from 19:44 to 19:50 UTC, GitHub experienced a service outage with elevated error rates peaking at 1.30% of all requests, totaling approximately 1.16 million failed requests. This impacted 12 services across GitHub, including Pull Requests, Webhooks, Repos, OAuth, Git over SSH, Codespaces, and Gists. The incident was triggered by GitHub Enterprise Importer (GEI) making multiple, long duration queries which saturated a database connection pool. Recovery was seen at approximately 19:50 UTC once the migration's calls stopped; GEI migrations were reenabled at 23:32 UTC after a code fix was merged.

We have completed a detailed root-cause review and are implementing improved database-health safeguards. We will continue to review and add additional safeguards to prevent future recurrence.

updates.body:
On October 7, 2026, GitHub had two outages of write operations with the same cause, totaling about 19 minutes. The first ran from 15:06 to 15:16 UTC (about 10 minutes) and the second from 16:52 to 17:01 UTC (about 9 minutes). In both windows, actions that save or change data failed across Git operations, pull requests, issues, GitHub Actions, the API, webhooks, sign-in and authentication, GitHub Apps and OAuth, code scanning, Codespaces, and Copilot. Reading data was largely unaffected.

In the first outage, 5.6% of all web and API requests failed, peaking at 8.9%, and more than 12,000 organizations saw failed requests. Up to 26% of Git authentication requests failed, and 17% of Actions workflow runs failed with infrastructure errors. In the second outage, 6.2% of web and API requests failed, peaking at 9.3%, and more than 11,000 organizations were affected. Up to 25% of Git authentication requests failed, and 19% of Actions workflow runs failed. No databases experienced data loss, and operations retried after recovery succeeded.

GitHub relies on an internal service that keeps track of which database servers should receive new and updated data. While replacing machines that run this service as part of regular maintenance, one of the new machines started with an outdated copy of its records, which still listed database servers we had already retired. When this node came online, it incorrectly modified routing configuration with the outdated records, routing write requests to non-existent database servers.

Each outage ended when one of our established machines with correct configuration became the leader of the quorum and sent the correct configuration. After the first outage, we identified the new machine as the source and paused automated maintenance to stop it from being leader again. At 16:52 UTC, an automated maintenance task that did not honor the pause put it back in charge, and the outage happened again. We shut that machine down at 17:02 UTC and have since removed it, and the automation now honors the pause, which was a new regression due to an update of our puppet infrastructure.

To prevent recurrence, we are clearing retired database servers from the service's records before any new machine is added, and we are keeping new machines from being elected leader until their records have been checked. We are also changing our systems to reject configuration that point to servers that don't exist and to keep using the last known-good settings instead. Finally, we are giving responders a faster way to take a misbehaving machine out of service, and adding alerts so changes like this are spotted within seconds.

We will share a more detailed write-up of these incidents in our monthly availability report, along with the status of the repairs we are making to prevent issues like these in the future.

updates.body:
On October 12th 2026 11:51 UTC GitHub experienced elevated 500 responses across several application pages. This caused failures on Issues and Pull Requests as well as Projects and Actions. Customers also experienced delayed notifications in their web inbox and via email.

The immediate impact to Issues, Pull Requests, Projects, and Actions was mitigated by 12:41 UTC on October 12th. Notifications deliveries to the web inbox and via email were recovering at 15:27 UTC and fully mitigated by 20:16 UTC.

The incident was triggered through a latent condition in our notifications delivery pipeline that put a high volume of an expensive query on our sharded database replicas. This reduced available database capacity to serve requests for Issues, Pull Requests, Projects, and Actions.

We have fixed the notifications pipeline’s code path that issued the expensive query. We are also improving resilience of the database layer to reduce the likelihood and impact of similar incidents.

updates.body:
On October 19, 2026, between 15:24 and 16:52 UTC, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages, and webhooks generated by Actions were degraded. Live updates on GitHub.com and code search were also degraded for part of this time. No data was lost.

Impact

- Workflow status updates, logs, and checks were delayed.
- 5.13% of jobs on GitHub-hosted runners were delayed in starting, and 0.02% of workflow runs failed.
- During the first 30 minutes, 8.47% of requests to the Actions jobs REST API returned errors.

Pages deployments and webhooks generated by Actions runs were delayed.

An internal Actions service that stores logs and run status lost connections to some of its cache servers in one cloud region and immediately retried them from every server at once. The resulting surge of new connections overloaded a shared network link between our data center and that region, which also disrupted other services that use the same link. We mitigated the incident by moving the Actions service off the affected cache servers and reducing connections from other services on the link. We then processed the delayed Actions work. We are continuing to investigate the cause of the initial connection timeouts.

We were already in the process of rolling out a limit on how quickly this service can open new connections, but it was still in shadow mode (logging only, not enforcing) at the time of the incident. We have since fully enforced it and capped the service's concurrent connection attempts. We are extending these limits to other Actions services, adding backoff to retries, limiting how much shared network capacity a single service can use, and improving alerting so we can find the source of connection surges faster.

updates.body:
On October 21, 2026, between 13:22 UTC and 19:22 UTC, several GitHub services were delayed due to degradation of our internal event streaming platform.

Pull request updates, push webhooks, and push-triggered Actions workflows were delayed by up to 33 minutes until 15:36 UTC. Actions status updates were delayed by up to 33 minutes until 16:16 UTC, holding up some merges and deployments that wait on checks. Webhook deliveries and live updates were delayed by up to 25 minutes until 16:52 UTC. Audit log events were delayed by up to two hours.

This was due to servers in the platform running out of memory caused by client reconnections without sufficient retry backoff. We mitigated the incident by moving the busiest workloads to less-loaded servers and adding capacity.

We have since added reconnection backoff and added server capacity. We are building a solution for auto-rebalancing connections across servers, and splitting the platform into smaller, isolated clusters to reduce blast radius and time to mitigation of issues like this one in the future.

updates.body:
On October 22, 2026, from 13:05 to 15:20 UTC, our event streaming platform was degraded resulting in elevated job processing latency spikes of 19-35 seconds and elevated job processing times of 4m – this resulted in delayed Actions workflow and step results (up to 13m), notifications (20m) and repository push events (12m). Recovery for repositories began at 14:32, with Actions recovery beginning at 14:59. The issue reoccurred at 16:26 again impacting Actions runs, repo push events, and notifications. Recovery began at 17:16 and completed at 2:07.

The incident was caused by a significant increase in load coupled with client connection storms during a deployment overloading our Kafka event streaming brokers.

To prevent future recurrence, we have expanded the affected cluster, shifted traffic to less loaded clusters, and implemented tunable client reconnect backoff.

updates.body:
On October 22, 2026, between 14:55 and 17:28 UTC, search on GitHub.com was degraded. Search-backed features in Issues, Pull Requests, Projects, Actions, Packages, and some REST API endpoints returned errors or incomplete results. On average, 21% of search requests failed, peaking at 52%. Running Actions workflows, uploading and downloading packages, and Git operations were not affected.

This was due to the proxies that route requests to our search clusters running out of CPU while setting up encrypted connections. Requests that timed out were retried, which added more load and kept the proxies overloaded. The search clusters themselves remained healthy.

We mitigated the incident by adding proxy capacity, after which search recovered at 17:28 UTC.

We have started reducing the CPU cost of these encrypted connections. We are also working to make search retries adjustable during an incident without a deployment, and to alert on search failures sooner. Together these will reduce our time to detection and mitigation of issues like this one in the future.

updates.body:
On October 23, 2026, between 07:06 UTC and 07:27 UTC, GitHub Actions workflow run results were delayed. Job status, check run updates, and logs in the GitHub UI and API updated with an average delay of about 2 minutes, and some updates were delayed by up to about 7 minutes.

During this window, a storage dependency that Actions uses to process workflow logs and artifacts throttled our requests. This slowed result processing, causing updates to queue up. The queue was fully processed by 07:27 UTC, shortly after the throttling stopped.

To reduce the risk of recurrence, we have added several storage accounts to increase capacity, and we are working on additional steps to continue to scale. We are also working with our storage provider to understand why the throttling occurred, and improving how result processing handles storage throttling and how quickly we detect it.

On October 26, 2026, between 17:52 and 18:49 UTC, some customers experienced slower response times across the Checks API, Issues, Pull Requests, GraphQL, Notifications, and related services. Impact was limited to requests served from one of our datacenter sites. Some GraphQL requests failed, and some notifications were delayed. Among GraphQL requests served from the affected site, the average error rate was 5.68%, with a peak five-minute error rate of 14.32%.

Unusually large requests for contribution history overwhelmed part of our database infrastructure, causing a backlog. Requests continued reaching the slow component rather than being redirected to healthy systems. Restarting the component restored its performance. The incident was marked mitigated at 18:46 UTC and resolved at 18:57 UTC.

We are adding limits to these requests, improving alerts to detect overload sooner, and strengthening automatic redirection to healthy systems.

incidents.title: Elevated 404s for GitHub App s2s tokens in git/API

updates.body:
Between 0655 and 0801 UTC on 10/27, customers experienced increased failure rates for API and git requests authenticated with server-to-server tokens for GitHub Apps (excluding Actions tokens). During this window, authenticated git operations mistakenly returned 404 for 1.24% (2.6x) of requests on average and 2.49% (5.3x) at peak.

These failures were caused by a scheduled maintenance event where GitHub migrated 7 tables between two MySQL clusters in our IAD and Azure Central US datacenters. One of the affected tables stores installation records for GitHub App server-to-server tokens (excluding Actions). We've successfully completed several of these migrations in recent months without notable customer impact. However, in this case, the migration coincided with a scheduled cleanup job on the installation records table, which deleted approximately 59 million records from 0444-0617 UTC. As a result, the gh-ost tooling used in the migration experienced inter-cluster replication delays (up to 1 hour at peak).

At 0655 UTC, we begin transitioning reads of the target tables to the new MySQL cluster, with 100% of reads cutover at 0721 UTC. Customer impact began, but was not detected, throughout the read cutover and persisted until completion of the write cutover at 0801 UTC. We are updating our processes and automation to prevent a repeat of this incident, including disabling overlapping cleanup jobs prior to these migrations and blocking the cutover of reads when replication delays are high.

incident_updates.body:
Between 0655 and 0801 UTC on 10/27, customers experienced increased failure rates for API and git requests authenticated with server-to-server tokens for GitHub Apps (excluding Actions tokens). During this window, authenticated git operations mistakenly returned 404 for 1.24% (2.6x) of requests on average and 2.49% (5.3x) at peak.

These failures were caused by a scheduled maintenance event where GitHub migrated 7 tables between two MySQL clusters in our IAD and Azure Central US datacenters. One of the affected tables stores installation records for GitHub App server-to-server tokens (excluding Actions). updates.body:
On October 28, 2026, between 13:52 and 15:24 UTC, Copilot users saw errors when using several GPT-family models and the MAI Code 1.1 Flash model. Affected experiences included Copilot Chat in IDEs and on GitHub.com, the Copilot CLI, Copilot Code Review, the Copilot Coding Agent, Code Scanning Autofix, and Code Quality. About 9.73% of requests to the affected models failed, with a peak of about 36.97% at the start of the incident.

The errors happened because a credential that we use to authenticate with an upstream model provider became invalid. We mitigated the incident by replacing the credential and redeploying the service. We are strengthening how we manage credentials for upstream providers to prevent this type of failure, returning retryable errors when an upstream provider rejects a request, and improving our monitoring so that we detect and mitigate this type of problem faster in the future.

updates.body:
On October 30, 2026, from 17:50 to 18:32 UTC, Actions, Pages, and Webhooks experienced degraded performance. Actions workflow processing, Pages deployments, and webhook deliveries were delayed, and code search and live updates returned errors. Some Actions queues took additional time to drain after mitigation, and the incident was resolved at 19:23 UTC.

The impact was triggered by maintenance on a cloud network gateway connecting an Actions service in the GitHub data center to Redis clusters in the Central US Azure region. The service's Redis client retried aggressively and redialed those connections. That produced a connection storm that saturated the gateway, with about 90% of connection attempts failing. Other services sharing the same network path were degraded as well.

We mitigated the incident by removing the affected resources from rotation, which ended the connection storm and allowed the gateway to recover. We have already reduced the number of connection retries in the impacted service and are further improving retry behavior with jittered backoff, shorter connect timeouts, and retry budgets. We are also working with our infrastructure team to make GitHub more resilient to gateway maintenance.

updates.body:
On November 3, 2026, between 12:34 and 13:51 UTC, some users experienced authentication failures and errors with the REST and GraphQL APIs, pull requests, Issues, and GitHub Copilot. On average, the error rate was 0.46% and peaked at 0.98% of API requests. Copilot API errors averaged 2.0% and peaked at 3.1%.

This was caused by a bug in our process for replacing control-plane servers in one of our compute clusters. When a replacement server did not receive a timely response from the existing cluster, it incorrectly created a separate cluster. This stopped traffic from reaching much of the cluster's capacity and overloaded the authentication servers that were still handling requests.

We mitigated the incident by removing the incorrectly configured server.
We are also fixing the replacement logic and adding safeguards to prevent servers in this state from serving traffic.

We mitigated the incident by removing the incorrectly configured server.

updates.body:
On November 3, 2026, between 15:00 UTC and 22:37 UTC, Git operations over HTTPS on GitHub.com were degraded. Clones, fetches, and pushes over HTTPS were slow, and some failed. For about half of Git HTTPS traffic, median response time rose from under 100 milliseconds to as high as 5 seconds. On average, the error rate was 0.65% and peaked at 1.29% of requests to the service. Git operations over SSH were not affected.

This was due to a buildup of excess connections on the hosts that serve Git HTTPS traffic, which saturated their network capacity and caused slow and failed responses for all clients served by those hosts.

We mitigated the incident by blocking a client traffic pattern at our load balancers and reloading them, which released the excess connections. The block also prevented some users of one third-party integration from performing Git operations over HTTPS until we removed it on November 4 at 13:26 UTC.

We are working to alert on sustained Git HTTPS latency sooner and make load balancer mitigations take effect on existing connections immediately.

On November 4, 2026, between approximately 03:40 UTC and 10:01 UTC, some Copilot agent users experienced errors listing and creating agent tasks. On average, 1.22% of requests were failed, with a peak of 2.68% over a ten-minute interval.

The issue occurred when increased task-list traffic and expensive queries exhausted shared database capacity. We mitigated the broader impact by disabling a client experiment and temporarily restricting task-list requests from the affected client. Task-list requests remained restricted after the wider service recovered; we removed the blanket restriction on November 6 and continued a gradual rollout.

We’ve since improved task-list queries, moved rate limiting to separate infrastructure and added capacity monitoring. We’re continuing to reduce unnecessary client requests and validate capacity before expanding the rollout to reduce the chance of recurrence.

updates.body:
n November 4, 2026, between 09:35 UTC and 11:43 UTC, customers experienced intermittent errors and timeouts across GitHub.com, primarily on actions that write data. At peak, about 20% of pull request write operations (such as merging, commenting, and reviewing) failed, along with about 10% of issue creates and edits and 10–15% of project item edits. Git pushes over SSH, REST and GraphQL API requests, code scanning uploads, releases, and package operations were also affected, and about 1% of Actions runs were delayed by more than five minutes or failed to start. Overall, nearly 4% of all requests to GitHub.com failed at the worst point. Reads were largely unaffected, and retrying a failed action a short time later usually succeeded.

The incident was triggered by a burst of concurrent updates to the same database record, which tied up all available connections to one of our primary databases. Although that contention cleared, the backlog of waiting requests kept our database connection layer overloaded, and it did not recover on its own. We mitigated the incident by failing over to a new primary database host. Most services recovered by 11:31 UTC, and Actions recovered by 11:43 UTC.

Since the incident, we have disabled the code path that triggered the contention, increased the processing capacity of our database connection layer by 50%, and added alerting to detect this type of overload earlier. We are also improving our procedures so we can fail over sooner in similar situations.

updates.body:
On November 4, 2026, between 15:49 UTC and 16:48 UTC, and again between 17:20 UTC and 17:55 UTC, GitHub Actions, Pages, Webhooks, Code Scanning, and Copilot coding agent experienced delays. During this time, Actions workflow runs and job status updates were delayed by up to 25 minutes. Pages deployments dropped to about 4% of normal volume, webhook deliveries dropped to about 58% of normal volume, and Code Scanning analyses and Copilot coding agent sessions were delayed. Delayed events were processed after mitigation.

This incident was caused by a configuration change to an internal event-routing service that unexpectedly paused delivery of several event streams. The change depended on feature flags that were not set up as intended, which the service did not handle gracefully. We mitigated the first period by rolling back the configuration change at 16:14 UTC. The code change itself was not reverted by the rollback, so a subsequent deployment reintroduced it. We mitigated the second period at 17:40 UTC by rolling back again, then processed queued events and cleared backlogs.

We are taking several steps to prevent a repeat. The routing service will keep its existing behavior when a feature toggle is missing, so a misconfigured flag can no longer pause delivery. We are adding a pre-deploy check that each routing flag exists and is registered under the correct owning service, and we are making flag ownership less error-prone to set. We are also improving alerting so we detect paused event delivery sooner.

Between 16:39 and 16:57 UTC on November 5, 2026, some customers experienced failures starting workflow runs in GitHub Actions and Checks, and some in-progress runs failed. At peak, about 3% of workflow runs failed to queue, and roughly 0.21% of in-progress runs failed.

The cause was resource exhaustion in a database service that stores Actions Checks data. Bursts of highly concurrent, large read requests put the service under memory pressure, which caused it to stall and reject requests.

We mitigated the incident by failing over the affected database host. To prevent a recurrence, we have increased memory capacity across the affected database fleet. We will also be limiting concurrency of large queries to prevent heavy read traffic from causing a broad failure of critical workflows.

On November 5, 2026, between 23:21 and approximately 23:26 UTC, several GitHub services experienced elevated errors, including Git operations, Issues, Actions, authentication, and API requests. Customers may have encountered failed requests and Git pushes, and some Actions workflow runs were delayed.

This incident was caused by a bug in our database failover automation during planned maintenance. The automation stopped before completing the switch to a replacement database primary, leaving the existing primary unable to accept writes. We mitigated the disruption by restoring writes on the original primary. We subsequently completed the maintenance and monitored services to confirm recovery.

We are fixing the automation bug and strengthening our pre-maintenance checks and recovery procedures to prevent similar disruptions and restore service more quickly if a failure occurs.

updates.body: On November 9, 2026, GitHub.com experienced intermittent timeouts between approximately 05:10 and 08:15 UTC. Across that full window, 6.5% of recorded requests to github.com timed out, with a five-minute peak of 13.9% between 07:40 and 07:45 UTC. Release downloads were more affected: 38.5% of recorded requests timed out, peaking at 76% during that same five-minute interval. The two main error waves lasted about two hours and ten minutes in total, with recovery between them. The errors affected repository browsing and disrupted some CI workflows and Copilot code review jobs. Contrary to our earlier updates, follow-up analysis confirmed at least 6,236 authenticated requests that timed out, affecting activity feeds, access to uploaded attachments and repository archive downloads. Errors occurred during elevated traffic to our web infrastructure that handles unauthenticated requests. Impact was mitigated when traffic causing pressure on this system was alleviated. Our follow-up work focuses on improving capacity monitoring, traffic prioritization improvements, and automated protection against traffic spikes.
